title: Ridgley split and Celestin's 1949 Paddock comeback
summary: The dollar dispute that split the Tuxedo bands and the comeback band that opened at the Paddock in 1949.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Not with me. Not on the records. Shots never didn't leave Ricard. Shots was stuck with Ricard. He stayed with Ricard. Shots and this boy, uh, but this boy, uh, played trombone. Well, they all stuck with Ricard. Yeah. David Jones and them, they stayed on the Pelican with Ricard. Emma Barris, all them John Porter, they all stayed with Ricard on the Pelican. Yeah. Papa Celestine and David Ricard fell out for one dollar. Really? That's right. That's why they made the split. They won one large dollar. That's why they made the split. So Papa made his band. That's why they made two Tuxedo bands. Celestine Tuxedo bands and Rizzley Tuxedo bands. So finally, Rizzley's already existing now, but still living. Yeah. Papa, he's gone forever. So we did fine with Papa's new big band. And we went on through and I just settled down. Here and then, got married and stuck around and the pressure comes through. In and out, in and out, you understand? Working in and out, gig work, play every place around. I knew all these you could play. And the boy started splitting up. Guy went away and Paul Bones went away, you know. So I just split up like that. So I just made a great change. So, and things was really dead, dead, dead, me and Happy. We stuck with Celestine. All the big time, they had them quit. So Papa said, I'm going to make a comeback. I said, what you going to do now? I was waiting at the shipyard then. So I said, he's going to make a comeback. So yeah, let's get through together and make a rehearsal. I said, now what you going to do now, man? So my wife said, oh man, you are, told him over the telephone. Oh man, you ought to go sit down and rush your noise. My same little wife in the back there. So he just laughed over the telephone. So we made a couple of rehearsals. We got Ricard on bass, Piku on clarinet, and myself on trumpet, and Pop on trumpet, Black Happy on drums, and Moistad D Fields on piano. That was the comeback band. Yeah, we rehearsed that pop. I rehearsed it twice, three times a week. So finally, Pop made a comeback, and Johnny Corrin started the book and Papa Celestine. And we got together and started coming back, coming back, coming back, grassland. So there Pop, Celestine, Ricard got a job at the paddock, where his little brother was working. His little brother Lester played drums. He had a combo there. He had a job at the paddock and said, Mr. Villaner wanted to try a Dixley band. Who could I get in touch with? So he brought Ricard to see him, Mr. Villaner. And Ricard called me up 12 o'clock that night. So he got a job, man, on Bourbon Street. That was in 49. That was around May the 10th. May the 8th or 9th. So we're going to start Saturday night. So that was on May the 10th. So I was taking Papa Celestine, myself, and Happy. And we had to get a good Dixland piano player. And he didn't want no women to play piano. So Ricard said, I'm going to get Octave Crosby. So Celestine said, you get who you want. I'm not going to leave my band out here. I'm not going to play there to help you to build it up. That's what he said, because I got too much work coming up. He said, Billy, you going to be with me? You and Happy. I said, yeah, we're going to come. We ain't going to leave. It's like that. So things went on the first six months at the paddock. Celestine worked on the Ricard. So, let's start working on the Ricard.
